I ran `/code-conventions --review-pr` against `46ce83aa7...HEAD`: 5 files, +54/−7. I worked through every rule in the generated checklist (52 in all, none filtered out) and marked each one checked. The checklist went to the scratchpad, so no tracked files changed and I didn't run any tests.

**Rules that applied:** CHANGE-01, CHANGE-04, TYPE-01, TYPE-03, TYPE-04, REUSE-01, TEST-01, TEST-02, TEST-04, TEST-08, TEST-09.

**Zoom:** Level 1 only, on TEST-08. No review learnings are mapped to that rule, so I applied the rule's own wording. I didn't need Level 2 (GitHub source) for anything.

## Findings

**1. Medium · CHANGE-04: the public response contract changes type without versioning**
`src/modules/fees/routes/entities/fee-preview-response.entity.ts:12-13`
`FeePreviewTxData.chainId` changes from `number` to `string` in the response of the released `v1` route `POST /v1/chains/:chainId/fees/:safeAddress/preview`. That route shipped in #3019 on 2026-04-16. Any client doing `chainId === 1` or typed decoding will break without any error being raised. Using strings does match how the rest of the code base handles chain IDs. Still, the rule says this must be either versioned or explicitly backward-compatible. At minimum, the PR should confirm that web and mobile are ready for it and say so in the description.

**2. Low · TEST-08: redundant success assertion plus `if` guard**
`src/modules/fees/domain/entities/schemas/__tests__/tx-fees-response.schema.spec.ts:27-31` and `:48-52`
Both new tests use `expect(result.success).toBe(true); if (result.success) { ... }`, which TEST-08 names as a pattern to avoid. Assert on the parsed data directly instead, for example `expect(TxDataResponseSchema.parse(txData).chainId).toBe('1')`, or `expect(result).toEqual({ success: true, data: expect.objectContaining({ chainId: '1' }) })`.

**3. Low · TEST-01: fixture literals copied instead of using the existing builder**
Same spec file, `:14-23`, `:35-44`, `:61-70`
The same 8-field `txData` literal is written out three more times, even though `txDataResponseBuilder()` exists in the builder file this spec already imports from (`tx-fees-response.builder.ts:14`). Use `txDataResponseBuilder().with('chainId', '1').build()`. For the numeric and invalid cases, use `{ ...txDataResponseBuilder().build(), chainId }`.

**4. Low / nit · TYPE-01 / REUSE-01: inline chain-ID validation instead of the shared schema**
`src/modules/fees/domain/entities/schemas/tx-fees-response.schema.ts:8`
`z.coerce.string().regex(/^\d+$/)` is written inline, while the shared `ChainIdSchema` (`src/modules/chains/domain/entities/schemas/chain-id.schema.ts`) already exists and is used in 8 files. The difference looks deliberate: `ChainIdSchema` builds on `NumericStringSchema`, which accepts `'-1'`, and the new tests require that to be rejected. It also can't be a drop-in, because `ChainIdSchema` doesn't coerce numbers. Two options:
- Keep the regex, but add the `CHAIN_ID_MAXLENGTH` bound that `ChainIdSchema` enforces. The current regex accepts a numeric string of any length.
- Or add a one-line comment explaining why this schema differs.

Coercing with `z.coerce.string()` is fine on its own; the bridge entities already do it for `chainId`.

**No issues:** the builder change (integer-based ID, no leading zeros), the datasource spec update, SPDX headers on all touched files, and scope (CHANGE-01/02).

**Unresolved:** finding 1 needs the author to confirm the clients are coordinated. The fix may be a note in the PR description rather than a code change.
